claims.text: The initial Fe-Co-Ni-Ti high-entropy alloy is a single-phase fcc material.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti has coercivity below 20 Oe because of suppressed orbital moments and weak magnetic anisotropy.
Annealing in the 973–1273 K range can produce a Ti- and Co-rich B2-ordered secondary phase while retaining the fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix.
The proposed B2 phase will provide strong ferromagnetic exchange coupling.
The B2 phase will remain ferromagnetic over the proposed 300–500 K operating range.
A coherent or semi-coherent fcc/B2 interface will pin magnetic domain walls.
The ordered B2 phase has intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy that is less susceptible to orbital-moment quenching than the disordered fcc phase.
B2 ordering in Co/Ti-rich regions enhances the orbital-moment contribution by changing the local electronic environment.
Lattice mismatch and distinct magnetic anisotropy at the fcc/B2 interface enhance domain-wall pinning.
The dual-phase microstructure will overcome the orbital-moment suppression found in single-phase fcc systems.
The resulting dual-phase Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy will have coercivity exceeding 100 Oe.
The resulting dual-phase Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy will have a Curie temperature above 300 K.
Its saturation magnetization will be comparable to or slightly lower than that of the single-phase counterpart because of the secondary-phase volume fraction.
Related Cr/Mn-bearing fcc high-entropy alloys can exhibit paramagnetic and spin-glass regimes.
Antiferromagnetic interactions involving Cr can reduce the net magnetic moment in related Co-Ni-containing alloys.
The coercivity enhancement requires the secondary phase to remain below 100 nm and coherent or semi-coherent with the fcc matrix.
Coarsening or loss of interface coherency will lower coercivity by weakening interfacial pinning or producing large single-domain particles.
Ti content must be high enough to stabilize B2 ordering but low enough to preserve the fcc matrix.
It is uncertain whether Ti-Co interactions will favor B2 rather than L12 or another intermetallic under the proposed thermal treatment.
It is uncertain whether fcc/B2 magnetic coupling will be ferromagnetic or antiferromagnetic.
